article.story:
Pedro Neto scored twice in the second half to guide Chelsea to a 2-0 win at Everton on Saturday in a Premier League match marred by a serious-looking head injury to Chelsea goalkeeper Emi Martínez.

Morgan Rogers' eventful afternoon at Everton could have ended with a sending-off before half time but his good fortune was to Chelsea's benefit as the England forward delivered the key moment in a 2-0 victory.

The £117 million summer signing was already on a yellow card for a tussle with James Tarkowski when he went in studs up in a 50-50 with James Garner, catching his opponent high up on his shin.

It was a challenge neither referee Paul Tierney nor VAR felt warranted a second caution or even a straight red much to Everton's frustration and that turned to annoyance when the 24-year-old's driving run to the byline created the breakthrough for Neto 44 seconds after half time.

Rogers' later tumbling in the penalty area after brushing up against Tarkowski only enhanced his role as villain in the eyes of home fans.

When Neto slid home from Jordan Henderson's deflected free-kick for the first Premier League double of his career, the end of Everton's unbeaten start to the season was confirmed even with 11 minutes of added time still remaining.

However, it was not all good news for the visitors as they had goalkeeper Martínez carried off and taken to hospital after a clash of heads with Toffees centre-back Jarrad Branthwaite.

Belgian 21-year-old Mike Penders came on for a 25-minute Premier League debut and had the honour of not only becoming Chelsea's youngest goalkeeper in the competition but also helping secure their first top-flight clean sheet in 23 matches.

The 2-0 scoreline was harsh on the hosts, who were a match for their opponents having come to life midway through the first half when Harrison Armstrong was booked for a strong but fair-looking challenge on Josh Acheampong.

Prior to that Cole Palmer and Henderson had both tested Pickford from distance but conceded better chances as Merlin Röhl's shot saved by Martinez, who then conceded a corner for delaying the restart.

The goalkeeper was forced into a better stop to deny Thierno Barry who had half an empty net to aim at but directed his header straight at the Argentine, who also tipped over a Grealish shot which bounced into the turf and looked like dropping under the crossbar.

By then Rogers and Tarkowski had both been booked after the former responded to being barged to the floor off the ball by grabbing the Everton captain's shirt.

Moisés Caicedo smashed a brilliantly controlled volley against the angle of post and crossbar from Henderson's deep corner before the flashpoint of the game.

Rogers' lunging challenge on Garner left both writhing on the pitch but it was deemed not worthy of further action.

Pickford tipped over a Neto effort while they were still waiting for Garner to be allowed back on after treatment.

Chelsea's reputation as fast starters -- they have a league-high six goals in the opening seven minutes this season -- was enhanced as they scored a third goal inside the first four minutes of the second half.

Jorrel Hato sent Rogers running down the left and when he cut back Neto was left on his own in the penalty area by Vitaliy Mykolenko and was able to take his time before picking his spot inside the post with the ball creeping under Pickford's arm.

After Martínez's departure Penders showed he was not lacking confidence after charging to the edge of his penalty areas to punch away Garner's cross.

But Christian Noorgard's delayed Everton debut because of injury began with him losing possession on halfway, presenting Chelsea with a chance Neto reacted quickest to a loose ball to score.

articles.headline: Chelsea's Emi Martínez has surgery, will be 'back in a few weeks'
articles.description: Emi Martínez said he would be "back in a few weeks" after undergoing surgery following a head injury suffered during Chelsea's Premier League win over Everton on Saturday.

articles.headline: Liverpool come from behind to beat shorthanded Brentford
articles.description: Victor Muñoz and Alexander Isak take advantage of a weakened Brentford defence to score a pair of electric goals and lift Liverpool to a 2-1 comeback victory.

images.caption: Victor Muñoz and Alexander Isak take advantage of a weakened Brentford defence to score a pair of electric goals and lift Liverpool to a 2-1 comeback victory.

article.story:
Jordan Henderson was the unlikely hero as Chelsea's entertainers blew Bournemouth away in a comprehensive and chaotic 5-1 win at Stamford Bridge.

Former Liverpool captain Henderson, 36, scored two and set up one for Morgan Rogers while João Pedro also hit the net twice for the rampant Blues.

Xabi Alonso's side were two up inside three minutes to knock the stuffing out of a Bournemouth side still winless this season.

Their cavalier approach, to simply outscore their opponents, is unsustainable over a season, as evidenced by the three-game winless run before the international break which culminated in a torrid 3-0 defeat at Brentford.

True to form, after going 3-0 up they briefly gave Bournemouth a glimmer of hope by conceding a sloppy goal from a corner.

But further goals from Pedro and Henderson wrapped up a gloriously watchable romp in the October sunshine.

Cole Palmer, fresh from announcing he has signed a new contract until 2034, set the ball rolling when he sauntered forward unchallenged from the halfway line.

He swivelled in the penalty area and fed Henderson, who struck his shot first time in off the far post.

Chelsea attacked again straight from the kick-off and Pedro Neto was denied by Cherries keeper Djordje Petrovic before Henderson found Rogers, lurking on the left-hand side of the area.

The England star's curler took a deflection off the head of António Silva as it looped into the net, with just 149 seconds on the clock.

Shellshocked Bournemouth, who had lost just one of their previous 13 trips to London, eventually managed to regroup and almost pulled one back when Brazilian winger Rayan burst through.

He was denied by Blues keeper Emiliano Martínez, who reacted quickly to also keep out the follow-up from Ryan Christie.

But the Cherries were caught out by another lightning start by Chelsea at the beginning of the second half.

Just 40 seconds had elapsed when Neto skipped past Silva to the byline and pulled the ball back for Pedro to side foot home.

Five minutes later the Blues defence was breached when Moisés Caicedo attempted to clear a corner off the goal-line only to see it ricocheted back off Evanilson and into the net.

But in the 67th minute Chelsea had a fourth. Rogers fed Pep Chavarría down the left and his cross was snaffled up by Pedro.

Henderson then completed the scoring with a superb, curling free-kick to put the gloss on an emphatic victory for the Blues.

article.story:
Chelsea's winless run in the Premier League stretched to three matches as Brentford ran out deserved 3-0 winners at the Gtech Community Stadium.

It was a puzzling display for Xabi Alonso to ponder after watching his team impose themselves on the hosts in the first half yet struggling to find a goal threat, before succumbing in the second period to goals from Jaidon Anthony, Igor Thiago and Fábio Carvalho.

This was a Chelsea lineup containing all the elements of their summer transfer rethink with a solid experienced spine which saw Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck make first Premier League starts.

Something appeared to have clicked. They did not look half as chaotic defensively in the first half as they have done at times this season, standing up physically to Brentford, winning duels and not allowing Keith Andrews' side to dominate second balls.

Yet old habits had followed the visitors on their short trip across west London. The marking from Mikkel Damsgaard's 61st-minute corner was poor, Jannik Schuster headed on and Anthony finished it off, then Thiago was left free to score after Kevin Schade's shot was saved.

It was then a low cross from the German that was whacked in during stoppage time by Carvalho to send Brentford fans into dreamland.

The first chance went to Chelsea, Welbeck showing clever feet and laying the ball off for Pedro Neto, whose drive met a strong save from Caoimhín Kelleher.

The absence of João Pedro was hard to ignore through injury, his replacement Welbeck not quite so able to act as the middle link in a fluid trio with Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers.

Both forwards were involved and looked dangerous, but they operated far less in combination than when João Pedro is present.

Yehor Yarmoliuk had Brentford's only real sight of goal in the first half, bursting past the half-challenge of Rogers and shooting low into the gloves of Emiliano Martínez.

The visitors had a new midfield with Valentín Barco in for his first league start alongside Henderson. This was the former Liverpool captain's first appearance of any kind since coming on as a substitute for England against Panama in June, and he was a vocal, commanding presence alongside the Argentinian, who also impressed.

Further up, the Blues huffed and puffed. Rogers was afforded space inside the box to shoot late in the half, but his effort was well blocked by Schuster.

All their good work defensively was undone just after the hour mark when Damsgaard's corner found not one but two Brentford players unmarked. Rising highest to head back across goal was Schuster and Anthony had the simple job of nodding in from virtually on the line.

Another lapse handed Brentford their second goal. Levi Colwill and Wesley Fofana were parted by a simple through-ball by Damsgaard, sending Schade clear. His shot was kept out by Martinez, but Thiago was there to knock in his first league goal of the season.

There was a final flourish for Brentford when Schade drilled low across goal in stoppage time and substitute Carvalho arrived to blast into the roof of the net.

article.story:
Chelsea's chaotic start to life under Xabi Alonso continued with an entertaining 2-2 draw against Hull at Stamford Bridge.

It was a pattern that has become familiar in the early weeks of the season as the home side took the lead early on through Morgan Rogers and appeared to be cruising until another defensive implosion saw them give up command of the game and gift two goals to Hull's Mohamed Belloumi.

The first came after 28 minutes when Malo Gusto and Jorrel Hato each failed to take control of what should have been a simple mop-up job, allowing the Algerian winger to hammer in his first Premier League goal.

Emiliano Martínez then failed to deal with a corner and Belloumi drilled in via a deflection to put Sergej Jakirovic's side on course for another upset at half-time.

Chelsea tottered having again chucked away control of a match before their attacking prowess finally came to the fore once more to stave off an embarrassing home defeat.

Cole Palmer was again their saviour. He found space to dig out a cross for João Pedro to rifle home midway through the second half and spare Alonso's blushes.

Chelsea kept up their useful habit of scoring early. After seven minutes, Palmer fed Pedro, who swivelled and moved the ball to Rogers in space on the left. It was then far too simple a matter of Rogers skipping around Regan Slater and drilling beyond Konstantinos Tzolakis at his near post.

It took just one Hull attack for Chelsea's vulnerabilities to be exposed.

Gusto was hesitant in dealing with a long ball into the corner, then made a feeble attempt to prevent Ryan Giles from hoisting it into the box. Hato seemed not to know whether to attack the ball or to drop. He did neither and, as the ball bounced over him, Belloumi arrived to thump in the equaliser.

Only a good low stop from Martinez kept Giles from giving Hull the lead, but again Chelsea's defensive shape was awful. They would be made to pay almost immediately.

Semi Ajayi headed the resulting corner against the bar with Martinez flailing and the ball came out to Belloumi, whose driven effort was deflected in.

Chelsea had by now let in 12 goals in Alonso's five-and-a-half matches in charge.

Equally alarming was that frailties at the back appeared to be undermining efforts elsewhere on the pitch. The midfield became a wild free for all and the fluidity in attack turned to misplaced passes seeking out mistimed runs.

Reece James' free-kick hit a post as Chelsea rallied in the second half.

Hull then lost Nobel Mendy following a clash of heads as he bravely prevented a certain goal for Pedro at the back post.

Martinez, signed to bring an end to the Blues' goalkeeping headache, spilled a straightforward shot from Slater, recovering just sufficiently to toe the rebound away from Oli McBurnie.

It fell to Palmer to drag Chelsea from their hole. It was his run to the byline and cut-back that found Pedro in space to hammer into the roof of the net for 2-2.

Tzolakis denied Rogers, who got in behind from Palmer's pass, then at the other end Martinez dived at the feet of Mohamed-Ali Cho, who should have won it for Hull.

articles.headline: Liverpool come from behind to beat shorthanded Brentford
articles.description: Victor Muñoz and Alexander Isak take advantage of a weakened Brentford defence to score a pair of electric goals and lift Liverpool to a 2-1 comeback victory.

images.name: Liverpool come from behind to beat shorthanded Brentford
images.caption: Victor Muñoz and Alexander Isak take advantage of a weakened Brentford defence to score a pair of electric goals and lift Liverpool to a 2-1 comeback victory.

articles.headline: Mikel Arteta: 'Big believer' Arsenal's Kai Havertz can score 30 goals a season
articles.description: Mikel Arteta has said he is a "big believer" that Kai Havertz can be Arsenal's 30-goal-a-season man.

images.name: Kai Havertz  [1296x729]
images.caption: Kai Havertz has started of all of Arsenal's Premier League matches so far this season.

images.name: Arteta happy with Arsenal's 'great attacking flow'
images.caption: Arteta happy with Arsenal's 'great attacking flow'

article.story:
Arsenal needed to come from behind to win a breathless game 2-1 against Chelsea at the Emirates Stadium as Kai Havertz scored for the third time in the Premier League against his former club.

Havertz netted midway through the first half to equalise after Morgan Rogers, who the champions missed out on signing during the transfer window, had stunned home fans with a volleyed goal after 77 seconds.

The Germany international was instrumental too in Martin Ødegaard's 50th-minute winner, executing a delightful dummy to leave Chelsea's defence flatfooted and create room for the captain to rifle home.

Chelsea had lost four league games in a row at the Emirates, conceding 11 goals, but here they gave Arsenal a far sterner examination than at any time during that sequence, with the front three of Cole Palmer, João Pedro and Rogers again showing their potential as assets in a possible title challenge.

Yet Xabi Alonso appeared no closer to solving the enigma of a team so irresistible in attack yet too easily pulled into all the wrong shapes defensively and in midfield.

In truth, Arsenal's play and Chelsea's wobbles ought to have brought victory by a larger margin, Emiliano Martínez with a wonderful stop to deny Bukayo Saka, before David Raya gave a reminder of his own indispensability with an even better save to keep out Estêvão.

The Emirates was silenced with a Chelsea goal in the second minute.

Arsenal wasted multiple chances to deal with Reece James' deep free-kick. Declan Rice's header failed to clear the box, Odegaard was beaten to the second ball, and waiting on the edge of the box was Rogers to send a volley back and just beyond the reach of Raya, who may have been slow to get down.

A goalmouth scramble ended with Riccardo Calafiori putting the ball in the net before VAR spotted an offside against Ezri Konsa somewhere amongst the muddle of shots, ricochets and blocks.

Martinez saved from Saka after a lovely ball to release him by Odegaard, then Wesley Fofana had to be alert to deflect behind Havertz's first-time strike.

James and Palmer both had worthy attempts from range saved by Raya.

Chelsea continued to threaten, with Pedro inches away from making it 2-0, sliding in at the back post narrowly short of Palmer's cross.

All of Arsenal's danger was coming down the right and it was from there that they levelled. Havertz received the ball out near the flank and ran it infield through too little Chelsea resistance, sending a low shot between the legs of Maxence Lacroix that beat Martinez at his near post.

Arsenal were fortunate not to go in at the break behind, Pedro Neto burning down the right, cutting inside and striking a post.

The winner for Mikel Arteta's side was beautifully worked. Christos Tzolis collected the ball wide and slipped a pass into the box that was cleverly allowed to run on by Havertz, his feint allowing the ball to reach Ødegaard -- who lashed it home.

Chelsea were now penned, their defence full of gaps and struggling to contain the champions.

Only a wonderful reach from Martinez kept Saka's shot from creeping inside the far post. A stunning one-handed save from Raya denied substitute Estevao with a sublime curling effort, the closest the Blues came in the second half.

article.story:
Chelsea's winning start to life under Xabi Alonso continued with a pulsating 4-3 win over Brighton at Stamford Bridge.

It was another display of electrifying attacking football that should have had the game won inside half-an-hour, goals from Romeo Lavia, Pedro Neto and João Pedro putting the home side into a three-goal lead that was then almost dismantled by a brave Brighton fightback and their own clumsy defending.

Malick Yalcouyé crashed in his first goal for the Seagulls, beating goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez on his debut, then Joao Pedro's own goal had Chelsea teetering on the edge of an embarrassing collapse on the hour.

As often before in such circumstances, they turned to Cole Palmer. He took matters into his own hands to take the game away from the visitors and send Alonso racing down the touchline in celebration, bulldozing through midfield to lash in his team's fourth.

The question remains whether a title challenge is plausible while the Blues' defence remains this obliging. Most alarming was not that Brighton pulled back to within one goal, but the loss of control the team suffered when they came under pressure.

Even with the game won deep in stoppage time, Pascal Gross was given time and space to nod in an easy consolation goal.

There was no place in the Chelsea squad for Enzo Fernández, whose departure before Tuesday's transfer deadline appears increasingly likely, nor Robert Sánchez, whose errors in the win over Fulham may prove to be his last for Chelsea following the arrival of Martínez.

article.story:
Xabi Alonso made a winning start to life as Chelsea manager in a chaotic 3-2 win over Fulham at Craven Cottage.

It took only 31 seconds for João Pedro's goal to bring the visitors' new era to life, but despite an attacking display that was scintillating at times, plenty still remained of the defensive frailties that have undermined this team in the recent past.

Robert Sanchez's hopeless attempt to keep out Josh King's first-half equaliser was a reminder of areas of the pitch where Chelsea remain weak despite spending around £350 million ($477m) this summer.

That outlay included a record £117m lavished on Morgan Rogers. The England forward enjoyed an encouraging debut capped with a slotted finish to make it 2-1 before the break, then Cole Palmer, arguably Chelsea's best player on the night, began the second half with a beautiful finish to make it three.

Had Alonso had longer to work with his defence, Chelsea might have made lighter work of shutting the game down. Instead, they invited Fulham on, Sanchez fumbled again and Gonzalo García nodded in.

There was plenty here to encourage new boss Alvaro Arbeloa, though not every side he faces will be as defensively accommodating as Chelsea.

It had looked like being a long night. In the first minute, Jorge Cuenca's ball out of defence was headed back by Levi Colwill and allowed to run into the path of Palmer. His clipped pass found the run of Joao Pedro who finished stylishly as Bernd Leno advanced.

Chelsea looked nervous defensively, no-one more so than the goalkeeper. Sanchez almost made a mess of turning King's drive behind with a fumbled parry, but the next effort from the Fulham forward flummoxed him completely. Sanchez left too much room at his near post and was slow to get down, King's shot zipping between his flaccid wrists and in.

Joao Pedro volleyed a foot wide from Palmer's cross, Reece James drilled straight at Leno after Rogers' shot was blocked, then Leno deflected Romeo Lavia's close-range effort behind.

Chelsea re-took the lead before half-time and again Palmer was the architect. His neat ball down the right fed the onrushing Maxence Lacroix up from the back, and the defender drew the goalkeeper before picking out Rogers who slotted in.

Palmer had already showed sublime skill to beat four defenders and curl wide when, early in the second half, he made it three. Joao Pedro held up the ball inside the box and waited for the England forward to arrive. When he did, it was the simplest task to prod a finish between the legs of Leno.

Fulham were not beaten yet. It was 3-2 when Timothy Castagne beat Colwill and drew a save from Sanchez that was pushed straight onto the head of Garcia who bounced it in.

Antonee Robinson missed a glorious chance to complete the comeback when he lobbed wide with Sanchez caught out of his goal, then the goalkeeper partially redeemed himself in keeping out Ryan Sessegnon's fierce hit, as Chelsea hung on.
